title: Situation Summary: DR Congo: Cholera and Measles Outbreaks - 2013-2026
crisis: DR Congo: Cholera and Measles Outbreaks - 2013-2026
content:
• Between the start of 2026 and epidemiological week 16, DR Congo reported 22,487 suspected cholera cases and 642 deaths, with a case fatality rate (CFR) of 2.9%, marking a 20.3% increase in cases compared to the same period in 2025.  
• Cholera cases were reported across 189 health zones in 21 provinces in 2026, up from 98 health zones in 14 provinces in 2025, indicating wider geographic spread.  
• In week 16 of 2026 alone, 1,253 suspected cholera cases and 31 deaths were recorded in 95 health zones of 15 provinces, showing an 11.7% increase in cases from the previous week.  
• The cholera CFR has increased from 2.1% in 2025 to 2.9% in 2026, highlighting a worsening mortality trend.  

The ongoing cholera outbreak in DR Congo is intensifying both in terms of case numbers and geographic coverage, with a rising death rate. This situation underscores the urgent need for enhanced water, sanitation, and hygiene (WASH) interventions, as well as improved access to treatment and surveillance to control the epidemic and reduce fatalities.

title: Situation Summary: Somalia: Drought - 2015-2026
content:
• An estimated 5 million people in Somalia are affected by the ongoing drought, with widespread displacement, livestock losses, and rising malnutrition reported.  
• The failure of the Gu rainy season in Somaliland and Puntland has worsened drought conditions, expanding the crisis to additional villages and districts.  
• Early action interventions funded by the IFRC, including WASH support, multi-purpose cash distributions, and early warning dissemination, were implemented from early 2024 through mid-2025, with a second activation underway to scale up these efforts.  
• Rising river levels and flash floods have caused displacement and infrastructure damage, compounding humanitarian needs amid persistent drought vulnerability.  
• Increased fuel costs and commodity prices, driven by tensions in the Strait of Hormuz, are disrupting aid delivery and reducing purchasing power, worsening the humanitarian situation.  

Somalia’s drought crisis remains severe and multifaceted, with climatic shocks exacerbating food insecurity and displacement. Despite early action efforts, the combination of failed rains, flooding, and economic pressures continues to strain humanitarian response capacity and funding, underscoring the urgent need for sustained international support.

title: Situation Summary: Colombia
content:
• An estimated 1.5 million people in Colombia are at risk of flooding between April and June 2026, affecting 276 municipalities across 25 departments.  
• The highest flood exposure is expected in May and June, particularly in the Pacific, Andean, Caribbean, and Orinoquía regions.  
• Priority areas for flood impact include Chocó, Valle del Cauca, Cauca, the Magdalena River basin, and parts of the Amazon and Orinoquía regions.  
• Flooding is anticipated to result from river overflows and sustained rainfall during the rainy season.

Seasonal forecasts indicate a significant flooding risk in Colombia during the April–June rainy season, with widespread exposure across multiple regions. Preparedness and response efforts should focus on the identified priority areas to mitigate the impact on vulnerable populations.

title: Situation Summary: Iran (Islamic Republic of)
content:
• WFP is providing food and cash assistance to over 33,000 refugees in 20 settlements across Iran amid rising inflation and increasing food prices.  
• The ongoing Strait of Hormuz crisis is causing regional disruptions to food systems, trade routes, and humanitarian access, exacerbating fuel and food price inflation.  
• Humanitarian operations in Iran are affected by complex logistics challenges due to disrupted regional transport corridors, airspace, ports, border crossings, and fuel supply chains.  
• The crisis has broader regional impacts, with supply chain disruptions affecting neighbouring countries and complicating humanitarian responses.  

The deepening crisis in the Middle East, particularly around the Strait of Hormuz, is intensifying economic pressures and logistical difficulties in Iran. This is undermining vulnerable households’ access to food and basic needs, while humanitarian actors face significant operational challenges in delivering aid.

title: Situation Summary: Lebanon
content:
• Over 1 million displaced people are registered in Lebanon, with 125,621 internally displaced persons housed in 622 operational emergency collective shelters as of early May 2026.  
• Since 2 March 2026, there have been 2,702 fatalities and 8,311 injuries reported, with 321,666 Syrians and 68,712 Lebanese crossing back into Syria during this period.  
• Despite a formal ceasefire, military activity and attacks continue, including strikes in southern Lebanon, Nabatieh, Western Bekaa, and Beirut’s southern suburbs, undermining stability and civilian safety.  
• Healthcare services remain severely disrupted due to 155 attacks on medical facilities and personnel since 2 March, resulting in 104 deaths and 244 injuries among healthcare workers; multiple hospitals and primary health care centres are closed or operating with limited capacity.  
• Humanitarian access and the return of displaced populations are hindered by ongoing violence, movement restrictions, and security unpredictability, particularly in southern Lebanon, affecting the delivery of essential services including sexual and reproductive health and gender-based violence support reaching over 80,000 displaced people.

The situation in Lebanon remains highly volatile despite the ceasefire, with continued hostilities causing significant civilian harm and displacement. The protection of healthcare workers and facilities is critical, as is improving humanitarian access to meet urgent needs across affected regions.

title: Situation Summary: Libya
content:
• Armed conflict erupted on 11 May 2026 in Zawiya, Libya, involving two armed groups and local authorities, following similar clashes on 1 May 2026.  
• The violence has caused at least 1 death, 1 injury, and forced displacement of 82 people, who received immediate assistance from Libyan Red Crescent volunteers.  
• The security situation is rapidly deteriorating, severely restricting safe access and data collection, raising concerns about further escalation and repeated outbreaks.  
• Humanitarian volunteers have been directly targeted during the clashes, complicating aid delivery efforts.  
• Separately, during the first quarter of 2026, WFP assisted 145,265 vulnerable Sudanese refugees and host communities in Libya with food, nutrition, and cash support, but funding shortfalls mean only 25% of needs can be met for May and June.

The ongoing violence in Zawiya highlights the fragile security environment in Libya, which continues to impede humanitarian operations and exacerbate displacement. Meanwhile, existing vulnerable populations, including refugees, face reduced assistance due to funding gaps, underscoring the urgent need for increased support and protection measures.

title: Situation Summary: Somalia
content:
• The Shabelle River in Somalia is at moderate flood risk, with water levels rising significantly in Belet Weyne, exceeding the moderate flood-risk threshold by 0.25 m and showing a notable increase compared to 2025 and long-term averages.  
• Downstream areas such as Bulo Burte are also experiencing rising river levels, though still below the moderate flood-risk threshold, indicating ongoing flood water propagation.  
• Inter-clan conflict in Laashimo Valley, Sanaag Region, between Damalaxagare and Shimbiraale clans has displaced approximately 9,000 people (1,500 households), predominantly women and children.  
• The conflict stems from competition over scarce water and grazing resources amid drought conditions, with tensions exacerbated by unresolved revenge disputes.  
• Humanitarian access to Laashimo Valley is limited due to insecurity and longstanding hostilities, complicating aid delivery to displaced populations.

The situation in Somalia is marked by both natural hazards and conflict-driven displacement. Flood risks along the Shabelle River threaten agricultural livelihoods and infrastructure, while drought and resource scarcity are driving violent clashes among pastoralist communities. Humanitarian response is challenged by access constraints and ongoing insecurity in affected areas.

title: Jordan Operational Update - February-March 2026
content: OPERATIONAL CONTEXT In February, Barham Salih undertook his first official visit to Jordan as the United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees. During the visit, he reaffirmed UNHCR’s commitment to working with the Government, donors, and partners to support refugees and host communities, and to advance long‑term solutions. The High Commissioner emphasized that a significant number of refugees are expected to remain in Jordan for the foreseeable future, with many becoming increasingly vulnerable. In March, UNHCR closed its field office in Irbid after 12 years of serving refugees in northern Jordan. UNHCR maintains presence in the north through a newly established Irbid Field Unit which will continue to provide services to refugees with support from the UNHCR Country Office in Amman.

title: UNHCR Iraq Monthly Update, March 2026
content: CONTEXT As of the end of March 2026, Iraq generously hosts approximately 350,000 refugees and asylum-seekers, the majority (88%) of whom are Syrians. Close to 81% of this population resides in the Kurdistan Region of Iraq. While most refugees and asylumseekers live in urban and peri-urban settings, 26% remain in nine refugee camps across the country. Additionally, some 100,400 Internally Displaced People (IDPs) live in 18 IDP camps1 . UNHCR works with the Government of Iraq and partners to support refugee and asylum seeker access to protection and inclusion in public services, such as education and healthcare, as well as access to economic opportunities and in advancing solutions.

title: WHO’s response in the occupied Palestinian territory (January - December 2025)
content: CURRENT SITUATION Gaza Strip Throughout 2025, although hostilities were less intense during the two established ceasefires (January-March and October to present), the Gaza Strip experienced catastrophic destruction and continued deterioration of its health system. During the year, local health authorities reported 25 718 deaths and more than 62 852 injuries.
